title: kcdx verification report
description: The frozen cross-repo contract for the in-game verification report. Produced by the in-game kcdx verification test-suite plugin (a dev-mode console sweep run after a save loads, which writes the report alongside kcdx-dev.log); consumed client-side by the maintainer-tool frontend's verification worklist via the File API (no backend read seam). Every curated row gets its strongest applicable active attempt and a structured response — a verdict, the proof-strength rank that produced it, and an invocation-attempt record. The producer emits kcdx_id + resolved version + verdict + method_rank + invoke flags + detail per row; the consumer resolves the entity name from its own loaded DB by kcdx_id (a kcdx_id absent from the DB is the stale-report case the consumer surfaces). DURABILITY (the incremental-flush contract): the sweep flushes one row-result per line to disk the instant each row's attempt completes — never a bulk write at sweep end — so a mid-sweep death still leaves an ingestible report. This schema therefore validates BOTH shapes: a single per-row line equals exactly one rows[] element (validate it against the rows.items subschema), and the finalized document wraps the accumulated rows into schema_version + game_version + summary + rows[] plus the complete / rows_expected partial-report signal. A PARTIAL finalized document (complete:false, fewer rows than rows_expected — a sweep that stopped early) is a VALID report, not a malformed one.

schema_version.description: The pinned contract version. A consumer rejects a report whose schema_version it does not recognize. Frozen to the value 3 (the active-attempt model: the 7-state verdict enum, the method_rank proof-strength ladder, the invoke_attempted / invoke_skip_reason fields, and the complete / rows_expected partial-report signal).

game_version.description: The resolved game/DLL version the report was produced against (the version stamp). The version-applicability hash and reachability checks were run on the build that resolved to this version; the consumer shows it in the worklist and matches it against its DB version intervals. A free-form version string in the project's resolved-tag form (e.g. 'release_1_5_1164953_841' or '1.5.1164953').

summary.description: The roll-up the consumer's 'M/N passing' header binds. passing = count of rows in the verified block — verdict verified_working OR passed_not_verified (the strongest applicable attempt passed, whether or not execution was observed); total = count of rows in the report.

passing.description: Count of rows whose verdict is verified_working OR passed_not_verified (the verified block).

total.description: Count of rows in the report (== rows array length).

complete.description: Whether the sweep ran to the end of the curated set. true = every expected row resolved and was flushed (rows length == rows_expected); false = the sweep stopped early (a mid-sweep fault/hang/crash) and the report is partial. A partial report (complete:false) is a valid, ingestible report — the durability contract guarantees a complete-up-to-N report on any mid-sweep death; the consumer distinguishes it from a whole-set sweep by this flag.

rows_expected.description: The count of rows the sweep intended to attempt (the size of the curated set this run targets). The consumer compares rows length against this: equal with complete:true is a whole-set sweep; fewer with complete:false is a report that stopped early. rows_expected is the denominator the consumer can show against the rows actually present.

rows.description: One entry per curated row the in-game sweep attempted, in resolution order. Each element is also the per-row line shape the sweep flushes to disk as that row's attempt completes (one rows[] element per line); a partial report carries fewer than rows_expected of these.

kcdx_id.description: The curated entity id (== the address_names.id the engine plugins reference). The consumer resolves the entity name from its own loaded DB by this id; an id not present in the DB is the stale-report row the consumer flags.

version.description: The resolved address_versions version the row was checked at (the version interval the running build fell into for this entity). Free-form version string in the project's resolved-tag form.

verdict.description: The active-attempt verdict for this row — EXACTLY these seven snake_case tokens. A verdict is the CEILING of the strongest method that ran; only observed live execution (rank 1) earns verified_working, and every other passing attempt caps at passed_not_verified. verified_working = the function was observed executing correctly this session (a kcdx hook fired with correct pass-through, or kcdx's own production call already ran). passed_not_verified = the strongest applicable attempt PASSED (bytes / resolution / wiring) but execution could not be observed — passing tests, not proof-of-working. failed = an attempt the row should pass returned wrong (diverged bytes / dead resolve / wrong target / a thrown exercise). not_applicable = the running build's version is not covered by this row (the version check ran and found non-coverage — a gap). cannot_check = the attempt ran but the row lacks the inputs the check needs (no fingerprint, or a deferred kind such as vtable_index). skipped = a precondition was not met this run (needs a loaded save, run from the menu, module absent) — the only 'did not run', and it names why. error = the harness itself faulted on this row (the row is fine, the test blew up — distinct from failed).

method_rank.description: The proof-strength rank of the strongest method that actually ran for this row, weakest to strongest: 5 = existence/resolution; 4 = on-disk version-applicability hash; 3 = loaded-image reachability; 2 = safe-read exercise (a live value read with zero mutation); 1 = observed live execution (the function fired in the running process and passed through correctly). The report carries BOTH the verdict and the rank that produced it: a passing rank 2-5 caps at passed_not_verified; only rank 1 can award verified_working.

invoke_attempted.description: Whether the sweep actively invoked or exercised the target this run. false for an observed-execution row (the game calls it and the sweep observes — the sweep never mints a synthetic call to a foreign function) and for any row whose strongest applicable method was a static check. true only where the sweep performed a safe-read exercise (a zero-mutation live read). The 'could not safely invoke' fact is a structured property of the response (see invoke_skip_reason), never a verdict meaning 'gave up'.

invoke_skip_reason.description: When invoke_attempted is false, why no active invocation was performed — one of: unsafe_to_call (a foreign function the sweep must not synthetically call, e.g. the lua_pcall class — its strongest applicable attempt is the static check); uncontainable (an invocation whose side effects cannot be contained); not_a_callable_kind (a kind with no call ABI to invoke at all — a data slot, an anchor, a vtable entry). null when invoke_attempted is true (an exercise ran, so there is no skip reason).

detail.description: A free-text cause string naming what the attempt observed (the consumer renders it as the per-row detail line). Required and present on every row; the empty string is permitted (e.g. a clean verified_working row may carry no extra cause).

matched_address_version_id.description: The id of the address_version row whose fingerprint the swept bytes matched (the row attribution). Present on every row; an integer (>= 0) on a verified_working / passed_not_verified row, null otherwise. The in-game sweep tries each candidate address_version row's fingerprint (content_hash for a function, the per-kind datum otherwise) and records WHICH row matched; the importer uses this id to extend the matched row's interval forward when the swept version sat in a gap (a passing gap-pass grows that one row's coverage). The attribution invariant: a row in the verified block (verified_working / passed_not_verified) matched SOME candidate row, so it carries a non-null integer that names which; a failed / not_applicable / cannot_check / skipped / error row matched no candidate row, so each carries null. A verified-block row always names its matched row; every other verdict carries null. (The integer-or-null type + the verdict-conditional are enforced by the row-object if/then/else.)
